pairs.subject: visual-style-locking
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/library/style/[id]/_atelier/Atelier.tsx:208 The atelier changes a locked look only by duplicating it, shows the ratchet's refusal verbatim, lands no rejection without a note, shows a named send count apart from the window, and adopts a style into editable slots with the subject left for a person, so none of the 5 techniques judged here is a deviation.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/style/[id]/_atelier/Atelier.tsx:208 Duplicate is the only way to change a look, and the atelier then routes to the copy. A refused op shows the ratchet's own sentence (Atelier.tsx:94-95). The lock button appears only when view.lock.can, which the server computes. The kernel's lockBlocker demands zero undecided proofs and at least one approval.

app/(studio)/library/style/[id]/_atelier/Atelier.tsx:120 A rejection cannot land without a reason, and the wire door caps the note at one line (schema.ts note). The kernel refuses remove-proof on a rejected proof ('a rejection stays on the sheet', kernel styles test).

app/(studio)/library/style/[id]/_atelier/Dossier.tsx:105 The send count is the named constant SEND_REFS (4), separate from the window PROOF_CAP (14, approved only). This matches the rule that the window and the send count are different numbers.

app/(studio)/library/style/_port/fixtureActs.ts:96 Adopt reads the palette off a kept plate with the recognize model and splits the recipe into slots, leaving the subject for a person. Seeded plates land as undecided proofs and pass the gate like any other. Proofs then render on STYLE_TRIALS, never on the sample's subject. Dossier.tsx:47 shows the origin. This is the fixture side, a port of v1 adopt; the real side runs lib/foundry/adopt.ts.

app/(studio)/library/style/_port/schema.ts:19 The block is written only as the structured record (styleBlockSchema). The generate-proofs act runs lib/producers/style.ts, which compiles the block (compilePrompt) and attaches styleRefs on every proof call.

pairs.subject: visual-style-locking
pairs.evidence: lib/producers/scoutStoryboardActs.ts:126 Each of a storyboard's up-to-five Flux panels is drawn from the seat's free per-panel prompt. Kept cast identity blocks are compiled in, but no style block is: the storyboard's look exists only as a bullet the model never sees, so the five sibling frames each re-derive their own look.

techniques.evidence: lib/producers/scoutStoryboardActs.ts:126 The panel prompt goes to Flux as-is. The door (lib/foundry/scout/storyboard.ts castPanels) compiles only character identity blocks into panels. 'the look in words' is a bullet field and is not compiled per call. The still-to-clip hop does reuse the panel prompt, and the scene clip restates recipe motion, camera and light (scene.ts clipRequestOf).

lib/producers/scoutStoryboardActs.ts:122 This is the identity-sheet variant. Only a character's operator-kept portrait or sheet passes castStillOf as a reference, and a refused sheet fails the panel rather than drawing it unconditioned. Reference count is bounded by CAST_MAX, which is tied to FLUX_REFS_MAX.

lib/producers/scoutSceneActs.ts:189 A found scene is read keyframe by keyframe into a schema'd recipe (palette with jobs, camera, motion, lighting). The sample never reaches a generator as a reference. The human edit happens downstream: a kept look becomes a candidate style that is adopted and edited in the atelier.

lib/producers/scoutSceneActs.ts:148 Cut timing is measured over every frame by ffmpeg scene detection (instrument-routed), and each keyframe's timestamp is stated. But the instruction says 'Keyframe k of n' with n the picked count, not kept of available. Picks come from spreadEvenly/pickFrames with possibly irregular strides that go undeclared, and the reader is not told that removed frames are the sampler's doing.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard has no rule for scout-style exploratory batches: a small sibling set such as a five-panel storyboard, made before any project style exists. The 'throwaway exploration' exemption and the 'styled set' trigger both partly fit. A sentence on whether a per-candidate look bullet must be compiled into each frame would settle it.
